extracted.intended_audience: research authors and reviewers (working scientists) considering submissions to or participation in eLife peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and standards governing what eLife seeks to publish and how its peer review process is run, aimed at authors and reviewers submitting or evaluating manuscripts for the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired paper qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish papers that reviewers and editors find "authoritative, rigorous, insightful, enlightening or just beautiful."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife's goal is to publish highly influential research that demonstrates these qualities. Use these descriptors as high-level evaluative standards when preparing or reviewing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of content accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife publishes Research Articles, Short Reports, Tools and Resources, Research Advances, and various Magazine content (Editorials, Feature Articles, Insights, podcasts, interviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the Author Guide and Policies for details and requirements for each submission type; different types have different purposes and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Article length and figures policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Articles have no limits to the length or number of figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are not constrained by artificial length or figure limits for Research Articles; refer to the Author Guide for any other format-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection based on working scientists' judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife relies on the judgment of the working scientists who serve as editors to select papers for peer review and publication; there is no artificial acceptance rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions are made by active scientists rather than being driven by metrics such as a target acceptance rate or impact factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive and collaborative peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is intended to be constructive and collaborative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial decisions are delivered quickly; the process emphasizes collaboration between reviewers and editors to improve manuscripts rather than adversarial critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working scientists make editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Working scientists (serving as editors) make all editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This underscores subject-matter expertise and scientist-led judgment in handling submissions and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated, essential revision requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision requests are consolidated following an open, internal consultation among reviewers to deliver a single, concise set of the essential revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than multiple, possibly conflicting requests from individual reviewers, eLife aims to provide authors with one clear, prioritized list of essential revisions to guide revision efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review (transparency of review records)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-review decisions and author responses for published papers are available for all to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife makes review histories public for published papers to increase transparency and allow readers to see decision context, reviewer concerns, and author responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of editorial-process metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly updated metrics relating to the eLife editorial process are made available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers can consult these metrics (via the Author Guide) to understand timelines and other editorial-performance indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position on journal-level metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife does not support the Impact Factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a policy stance reflecting the journal's approach to evaluation and should inform authors' and reviewers' expectations about the journal's priorities.
